cells.tense: You are saying how things stand while they are still being sorted.
cells.act: let several things be true and act on one
cells.ask: This week, hold everything you can see as true without collapsing it, then move on the one that's ready — plainly, same day, edges unsoftened. What you didn't move on can keep.
cells.core: You can say how a thing stands while it is still being sorted, and it settles the room rather than splitting it. You carry the weight of something before you name it, so naming it lands as steadiness rather than as a verdict. Knowing a lot does not mean unloading all of it. Hold what you see together, choose among it, and move on one thing the same week. The rest will keep, and some of them will sort themselves while you are busy with the one. You do not need permission to say what is true, and you do not need to justify it afterward. Say it, act on it, and then let it sit where you put it.
cells.sheetLine: You can say what's true and hold the rest.
cells.verb: saying how a thing stands before anyone asks
cells.place: where you hold up under what is put on you

cells.tense: The shape gets declared before there is anything under it to stand on.
cells.act: follow the thought past where it is comfortable
cells.ask: Take what you are trying to make clear and stay with it longer than feels easy — beyond the place you could explain, until you reach what you actually grasp. Stop there, at that edge.
cells.core: You set the shape of things far ahead of when it needs setting, and the setting has become the work itself. You are already arranging how a thing will go so that nothing arrives unannounced. Underneath, there is a bracing against a future that cannot be written in advance, and the brace holds a position nothing is holding up. Depth is a better use of this than prediction. Go all the way into one hard thing, further than is comfortable, until your mind finds the edge of it. What you meet there is not a forecast of what happens next; it is what you genuinely understand, and that is something to stand on.
cells.sheetLine: You're declaring a shape nothing is holding up yet.

cells.tense: A shape was declared once, and you have been standing outside that door since.
cells.act: return to the work daily until it is profound
cells.ask: Go back to something you once put your weight behind and do today's piece — small, done the way you would if you meant to keep going. No announcement, no pace but daily.
cells.core: There is knowledge in you that used to come out as a claim, and now it stays quiet. The statement got made at some point and then went behind a closed door, and you have been waiting on the wrong side of it. People still lean on you and the leaning is real, but nothing you are building is feeding it, so the days get carried instead of shaped. That is not a failure of will. It is a place that has run low. Pushing harder will not fill it, and neither will announcing anything. Pick up something you already put your hand to and keep at it, daily, quietly, the way long work gets done. Build instead of declaring. The saying comes back through the making.
cells.sheetLine: You know what's true and have gone quiet about it.

cells.tense: You are holding the shape steady and calling it the way things happen to be.
cells.act: collect the fruit of the patient wait
cells.ask: Think of something that ended and took its time ending. Gather what it handed you — a few things, your words — and keep them. That gathering is the act; nothing has to follow it.
cells.core: The structure you carry is real, and you have been reading it as circumstance — something that happened to be the case rather than something you set. You are already saying how things are; the fact that you said it first gets filed under luck, or under what anyone would have done. You hold things level and credit the room. Go back to a change that has already finished and gather what it grew. Name what ended, count what it handed you. Your own claim is visible in what came out of it; saying so is only the last step of noticing what you did.
cells.sheetLine: You're calling your own structure circumstance.

cells.place: where you hold up under what is put on you
